title: Set the frame deliberately
scenario: An article about weekend baking needs a hero image: a loaf of bread on a kitchen counter, with clean space on the right where the headline will sit.
task: Decide shot scale, placement, negative space and aspect ratio — then compare with the reference version.

fields.label: Placement (where the subject sits)
fields.placeholder: on the left third of the frame…

fields.label: Negative space (what stays calm and empty)
fields.placeholder: empty counter surface on the right for text…

hints: The headline needs somewhere to live — reserve that space in the composition.
A ratio chosen first shapes every other framing decision.
explanation: Framing is four independent decisions: scale, placement, negative space and canvas. Stating them turns a lucky composition into a repeatable one — and when a result disappoints, you can change exactly one dial: “move the subject to the right third”, not “redo the whole prompt”. Reserving negative space is also a planning act: it is where real text will go.
sampleSolution: Medium shot of a rustic loaf of bread on a wooden kitchen counter, placed on the left third of the frame. Calm, uncluttered negative space on the right side where a headline can sit. Soft daylight from a window, warm editorial style. 16:9 wide header format.
